prompt.text:
Implement a small Rust-declaration generator in `solution.rs` using only the standard library.

Expose this exact API:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ModelType {
    Text,
    Integer,
    Decimal,
    Flag,
    Named(String),
    Sequence(Box<ModelType>),
    Dictionary(Box<ModelType>),
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Property {
    pub name: String,
    pub model_type: ModelType,
    pub required: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Model {
    pub name: String,
    pub properties: Vec<Property>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum GenerationError {
    InvalidIdentifier(String),
    DuplicateModel(String),
    DuplicateProperty { model: String, property: String },
    UnknownModel(String),
}

pub fn emit_rust_models(models: &[Model]) -> Result<String, GenerationError>;
```

Requirements:
- Valid identifiers are nonempty ASCII identifiers beginning with a letter or underscore and continuing with letters, digits, or underscores.
- Validate model names, property names, duplicate models, duplicate properties, and every `Named` reference before producing output. A reference may target a model declared later.
- Validation errors follow input order; within a property type, inspect recursively from the outside inward.
- Preserve model and property input order in generated text. Empty input returns an empty string.
- Emit each model as `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]`, followed by `pub struct Name {`, one indented public field per property, and `}`. Separate models with one blank line and end nonempty output with one newline.
- Type mappings are: `Text -> String`, `Integer -> i64`, `Decimal -> f64`, `Flag -> bool`, `Named(x) -> x`, `Sequence(t) -> Vec<t>`, and `Dictionary(t) -> std::collections::BTreeMap<String, t>`.
- A non-required property wraps its complete mapped type in `Option<...>`.
- Inputs must not be mutated.
- Do not include a `main` function.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
